definitions.explanation: A diplomatic representative of a country, ranking below an ambassador. Historically the chief representative sent to countries with which full ambassadorial relations had not been established.

examples.japanese: {公使|こうし}が{会談|かいだん}に{出席|しゅっせき}した。
{特命|とくめい}{全権|ぜんけん}{公使|こうし}として{派遣|はけん}された。
examples.english: He was dispatched as minister plenipotentiary.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}には{多|おお}くの{国|くに}に{公使|こうし}が{派遣|はけん}され、{外交|がいこう}{関係|かんけい}が{築|きず}かれた。
examples.english: During the Meiji era, ministers were dispatched to many countries and diplomatic relations were established.

notes:
Composed of {公|こう} (public, official) and {使|し} (envoy, messenger).

In modern diplomacy, most countries exchange ambassadors ({大使|たいし}) rather than ministers. The rank of {公使|こうし} is now less common but still exists in some diplomatic contexts and appears frequently in historical texts about the Meiji and Taisho periods.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {特命|とくめい}{全権|ぜんけん}{公使|こうし} (minister plenipotentiary)
- {公使|こうし}を{派遣|はけん}する (to dispatch a minister)
- {公使|こうし}{館|かん} (legation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公使|こうし}: minister (lower diplomatic rank)
- {大使|たいし}: ambassador (highest diplomatic rank)
- {領事|りょうじ}: consul (handles commercial and citizen affairs)
